groups.contract: Native connection cache publication precedes row callbacks and mutation APIs enqueue work
groups.disposition: All four complete exact pinned bodies personally read, not executed. Parsed transaction/committed reducer update applies the complete DbUpdate to locked client cache, releases cache then invokes row callbacks; pending callback/subscription/reducer mutations enqueue for processing before/after WebSocket messages. Successful invoke_reducer_with_callback means queued, not committed; actual callback separates Committed, real module rejectionString and internal failure. This supports first-party terminal submission/cause distinctions previously supplied NATIVE-PS-F038 at audit/records/final-acceptance-20261021/wave-01/producer-supplement-after-owner/native/findings.jsonl#37; no archived ownership transfer or lens coverage imported. Single connection advancer is explicit documented precondition; multiple parallel advancers can deadlock native receive locks, no current first-party misuse proven. frame_tick drains until queue empty with no per-frame work cap; unbounded producer/work starvation requires real supported input, not a new generic resource finding.

groups.contract: Connection lifecycle and pending operation failures retain native nontransactional seams
groups.disposition: Connecting/Connected/Ended gates connection callbacks and ensures one terminal callback. Identity token lifecycle becomes Connected before identity/connection-ID assertions and stores; mismatch is native protocol assertion, not a demonstrated server response. End sets send channelNone before callback and subscription disconnect hook. Pending Subscribe registers/start mutates handle before checking live send channel; reducer/procedure record callback before send presence check, so disconnected Err can retain pending registered state/callback. Caller must distinguish dispatch/ack/current connection and not retry blindly; no actual first-party failed-state leak proved here. Builder missing URI/database and malformed URI intentionally panic native preconditions, runtime/WebSocket initial I/O has typed FailedToConnect cause. Server parse errors become terminal SDKError; procedure return decode/unit reducer wire assertion can panic on native protocol violation. No claim of backend transaction rollback from client cache behavior or any live connection.

groups.contract: Native subscription cancellation has ordered state, but disconnect does not itself end handles
groups.disposition: Pending->Sent->Applied/Ended/Error status and unsubscribe_called jointly govern handle activity. unsubscribe sends pending mutation before setting flag/callback, preserving state on queue-send Err. Cancel-before-start skips Subscribe and unregisters with one end callback; applied/error/end take callbacks once. Actual on_disconnect is a no-op: it does not clear manager/client cache or mark Applied handles ended, despite introductory comment. Thus retaining a handle alone is not authoritative proof of live connection. Need actual first-party use after disconnect without connection freshness guard before promoting ordinary stale data/active status; no such witness here. Native IntoQueries clones or moves explicit strings and fixed arrays without numeric truncation; tests are compile-shape source fixtures only, not run.

groups.contract: Canonical SDK cause representation and global identifier counters retain boundary qualifications
groups.disposition: SDK Error/InternalError are Clone; InternalError stores optional Arc cause, Display prints it and deprecated cause() returns it, while source() explicitly returnsNone. This limits standard source-chain traversal inside the pinned SDK and does not justify early first-party to_string before retained state. Real module reducer rejection is BSATN String at actual native wire, distinct from immediate SDKError and callbackInternalError. Preserve actual canonical SDK types at first-party ports; no handwritten binding/dependency edits or invented Eq. NEXT_REQUEST_ID/NEXT_QUERY_SET_ID use global AtomicU32 fetch_add wrapping, with no in-flight uniqueness reservation on wrap; subscription registration rejects duplicate IDs. This is theoretical native lifetime/in-flight strengthening unless an actual supported request volume/collision is established, not an ordinary session collision. Concurrent cloning shares state intentionally; atomic ID acquisition alone does not prove aggregate callback lifetime.
